gavan-port-artura.scope: Reviewed the panorama’s caption and provenance, Hill 203’s connection with the fleet’s fate, and available evidence for the harbour’s names.

checks.title: What the Photograph Shows
checks.finding: The original caption confirms the western harbour from Golden Hill after the fortress fell. It does not show the sea entrance; the photograph’s 1905 date comes from the Commons catalogue.

checks.title: The Fleet under Land-Based Fire
checks.finding: NIDS connects Hill 203’s capture with the squadron’s destruction by fire from land. Sevastopol’s move, attacks and scuttling during capitulation were checked against Rodina’s study, rather than original reports.

checks.title: The English Name
checks.finding: An institutional account connects the name with Arthur and Ward in 1860. The naming record, exact month and damaged-ship story remain unchecked against a primary document.

checks.title: The Account of1371
checks.finding: China’s local-history website repeats the account of a safe crossing in 1371. It identifies no specific Ming-period document; this remains an attributed account rather than a verified renaming record.

sources.note: Date and identification follow the current record; upload history contains an earlier erroneous attribution to Hill203.
sources.rights: Commons: public domain in Japan and the US; NDL record: pdm. See the linked records.

ukreplenie-5.scope: Fortification No. 5: numbering, pre-war readiness, combat service and the limits of identifying surviving structures.

checks.title: The fortification and the fort were separate positions
checks.finding: The published readiness memo dated 1 December 1903 lists Fortification No. 5 as complete, Fort V as unfinished and Fort VI as newly begun. The original document has not been inspected.

checks.title: Surrender does not mean an absence of combat
checks.finding: Pilsudski’s published diary records Fortification No. 5 firing and receiving fire on 12–14 December 1904. The handover order establishes the surrender procedure, but does not prove that no separate assault occurred during the siege.

checks.title: Visible structures and the gun’s provenance
checks.finding: Modern photographs show a ditch and a large gun. Its model remains the field report author’s attribution; the photographs do not establish its provenance, Qing fabric or the structures’ dimensions.

checks.title: Survival needs a cautious explanation
checks.finding: The absence of a separate assault remains attributed to the channel. Present appearances alone cannot separate 1904 structures from later changes and restoration.

sources.inspection: Local metadata and two photographs of the ditch and gun inspected; the original post was not opened separately.
sources.note: Supports descriptions of visible structures and the author’s identification of the gun.
sources.rights: No individual open licence is recorded; the photographs bear the channel’s watermark.
